sanskrit: avyaktam āhuḥ prakṛtiṃ parāṃ prakṛtivādinaḥ tasmān mahat samutpannaṃ dvitīyaṃ rājasattama
english: The expounders of primal nature call the Unmanifest the supreme Prakṛti; and from it, O best of kings, there arose the Great Principle (mahat), which is the second.

sanskrit: ahaṃkāras tu mahatas tṛtīyam iti naḥ śrutam pañca bhūtāny ahaṃkārād āhuḥ sāṃkhyānudarśinaḥ
english: From the Great Principle comes the I-sense (ahaṃkāra), the third, so we have heard; and from the I-sense, the followers of Sāṃkhya declare, arise the five elements.

sanskrit: etāḥ prakṛtayas tv aṣṭau vikārāś cāpi ṣoḍaśa pañca caiva viśeṣā vai tathā pañcendriyāṇi ca
english: These are the eight sources of evolution; and the modifications are sixteen — the five gross particulars together with the five senses.

sanskrit: etāvad eva tattvānāṃ sāṃkhyam āhur manīṣiṇaḥ sāṃkhye vidhividhānajñā nityaṃ sāṃkhyapathe ratāḥ
english: Just this is the enumeration of the principles, say the wise ones learned in the rules and ordinances of Sāṃkhya, ever devoted to the Sāṃkhya path.

sanskrit: yasmād yad abhijāyeta tat tatraiva pralīyate līyante pratilomāni sṛjyante cāntarātmanā
english: Whatever is born from a given source dissolves again into that very source; in reverse order they are reabsorbed, and they are sent forth by the inner Self.

sanskrit: anulomena jāyante līyante pratilomataḥ guṇā guṇeṣu satataṃ sāgarasyormayo yathā
english: In forward order they come to be, and in reverse order they dissolve; constantly the qualities merge into the qualities, as the waves of the ocean into the sea.

sanskrit: sargapralaya etāvān prakṛter nṛpasattama ekatvaṃ pralaye cāsya bahutvaṃ ca yadāsṛjat evam eva ca rājendra vijñeyaṃ jñeyacintakaiḥ
english: Such is the creation and dissolution of Prakṛti, O best of kings: oneness in dissolution, and multiplicity when it sends forth creation. Thus, O lord of kings, is it to be understood by those who ponder what is to be known.

sanskrit: adhiṣṭhātāram avyaktam asyāpy etan nidarśanam ekatvaṃ ca bahutvaṃ ca prakṛter anu tattvavān ekatvaṃ pralaye cāsya bahutvaṃ ca pravartanāt
english: The Unmanifest is its presiding ground — this too is the illustration. The knower of truth sees the oneness and the multiplicity that follow upon Prakṛti: oneness in dissolution, and multiplicity in active unfolding.

sanskrit: bahudhātmā prakurvīta prakṛtiṃ prasavātmikām tac ca kṣetraṃ mahān ātmā pañcaviṃśo 'dhitiṣṭhati
english: Making itself manifold, it brings forth Prakṛti, whose nature is to generate; and over that Field the Great Self, the twenty-fifth principle, presides.

sanskrit: adhiṣṭhāteti rājendra procyate yatisattamaiḥ adhiṣṭhānād adhiṣṭhātā kṣetrāṇām iti naḥ śrutam
english: He is called the Presider, O lord of kings, by the best of ascetics; because he presides over the Fields, he is the Presider — so we have heard.

sanskrit: kṣetraṃ jānāti cāvyaktaṃ kṣetrajña iti cocyate avyaktike pure śete puruṣaś ceti kathyate
english: He knows the Field, the Unmanifest, and so is called the Knower of the Field; and because he lies within the city of the Unmanifest, he is also called the Puruṣa, the indwelling Person.

sanskrit: anyad eva ca kṣetraṃ syād anyaḥ kṣetrajña ucyate kṣetram avyaktam ity uktaṃ jñātā vai pañcaviṃśakaḥ
english: The Field is one thing, and the Knower of the Field is said to be another; the Field is declared to be the Unmanifest, while the Knower is the twenty-fifth principle.

sanskrit: anyad eva ca jñānaṃ syād anyaj jñeyaṃ tad ucyate jñānam avyaktam ity uktaṃ jñeyo vai pañcaviṃśakaḥ
english: Knowledge is one thing, and the object of knowledge is said to be another; the knowledge is declared to be the Unmanifest, while the object to be known is the twenty-fifth principle.

sanskrit: avyaktaṃ kṣetram ity uktaṃ tathā sattvaṃ tatheśvaram anīśvaram atattvaṃ ca tattvaṃ tat pañcaviṃśakam
english: The Unmanifest is called the Field, and likewise sattva, and likewise the Lord; it is without lordship and without selfhood, while the twenty-fifth is the true principle endowed with selfhood.

sanskrit: sāṃkhyadarśanam etāvat parisaṃkhyānadarśanam sāṃkhyaṃ prakurute caiva prakṛtiṃ ca pracakṣate
english: So much is the Sāṃkhya doctrine, the teaching of full enumeration; it carries out the reckoning, and it declares the nature of Prakṛti.

sanskrit: tattvāni ca caturviṃśat parisaṃkhyāya tattvataḥ sāṃkhyāḥ saha prakṛtyā tu nistattvaḥ pañcaviṃśakaḥ
english: The followers of Sāṃkhya, reckoning truly the twenty-four principles together with Prakṛti, hold that the twenty-fifth is free of those principles and stands beyond them.

sanskrit: pañcaviṃśo 'prabuddhātmā budhyamāna iti smṛtaḥ yadā tu budhyate ''tmānaṃ tadā bhavati kevalaḥ
english: As long as the twenty-fifth has not awakened its self, it is called the one who is awakening; but when it knows the Self, then it becomes the Absolute, alone and unconditioned.

sanskrit: samyag darśanam etāvad bhāṣitaṃ tava tattvataḥ evam etad vijānantaḥ sāmyatāṃ pratiyānty uta
english: Thus has the right vision been truly expounded to you; and they who know it in this way attain to oneness and equality.

sanskrit: samyaṅ nidarśanaṃ nāma pratyakṣaṃ prakṛtes tathā guṇatattvāny athaitāni nirguṇo 'nyas tathā bhavet
english: This is rightly named the demonstration, the direct apprehension of Prakṛti; these are the principles bound up with the qualities, while the Other, devoid of qualities, stands apart.

sanskrit: na tv evaṃ vartamānānām āvṛttir vidyate punaḥ vidyate 'kṣarabhāvatvād aparasparam avyayam
english: For those who abide thus there is no returning again; because of their imperishable being there is for them an undecaying state, free of mutual involvement.

sanskrit: paśyerann ekamatayo na samyak teṣu darśanam te 'vyaktaṃ pratipadyante punaḥ punar ariṃdama
english: Those of single-minded fixity may see, yet their vision is not perfect; again and again, O subduer of foes, they fall back into the Unmanifest.

sanskrit: sarvam etad vijānanto na sarvasya prabodhanāt vyaktībhūtā bhaviṣyanti vyaktasya vaśavartinaḥ
english: Though they know all this, yet for want of full awakening to the whole they will become manifest once more, falling under the sway of the manifest.

sanskrit: sarvam avyaktam ity uktam asarvaḥ pañcaviṃśakaḥ ya enam abhijānanti na bhayaṃ teṣu vidyate
english: All this has been called the Unmanifest, the All; but the twenty-fifth is not the All. For those who know him truly, no fear is to be found.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca sāṃkhyadarśanam etāvad uktaṃ te nṛpasattama vidyāvidye tv idānīṃ me tvaṃ nibodhānupūrvaśaḥ
english: Vasiṣṭha said: So much of the Sāṃkhya doctrine has been told to you, O best of kings; now learn from me, in due order, of Knowledge and Ignorance.

sanskrit: avidyām āhur avyaktaṃ sargapralayadharmi vai sargapralayanirmuktaṃ vidyāṃ vai pañcaviṃśakam
english: The Unmanifest, subject to creation and dissolution, they call Ignorance; and the twenty-fifth, free from creation and dissolution, they call Knowledge.

sanskrit: parasparam avidyāṃ vai tan nibodhānupūrvaśaḥ yathoktam ṛṣibhis tāta sāṃkhyasyāsya nidarśanam
english: Learn, in due order, of their mutual relation in ignorance, my son, as the seers have expounded the teaching of this Sāṃkhya.

sanskrit: karmendriyāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ vidyā buddhīndriyaṃ smṛtam buddhīndriyāṇāṃ ca tathā viśeṣā iti naḥ śrutam
english: For all the organs of action, the organs of perception are reckoned their knowledge; and for the organs of perception, the gross particulars are their knowledge — so we have heard.

sanskrit: viśeṣāṇāṃ manas teṣāṃ vidyām āhur manīṣiṇaḥ manasaḥ pañcabhūtāni vidyā ity abhicakṣate
english: For those gross particulars, the wise declare the mind to be their knowledge; and for the mind, they call the five elements its knowledge.

sanskrit: ahaṃkāras tu bhūtānāṃ pañcānāṃ nātra saṃśayaḥ ahaṃkārasya ca tathā buddhir vidyā nareśvara
english: For the five elements, the I-sense is their knowledge — herein is no doubt; and for the I-sense, the intellect is its knowledge, O lord of men.

sanskrit: buddheḥ prakṛtir avyaktaṃ tattvānāṃ parameśvaram vidyā jñeyā naraśreṣṭha vidhiś ca paramaḥ smṛtaḥ
english: For the intellect, Prakṛti, the Unmanifest, the supreme lord of the principles, is to be known as its knowledge, O best of men; and it is reckoned the highest ordinance.

sanskrit: avyaktasya paraṃ prāhur vidyāṃ vai pañcaviṃśakam sarvasya sarvam ity uktaṃ jñeyaṃ jñānasya pārthiva
english: Of the Unmanifest, they declare the twenty-fifth to be the supreme Knowledge; the All of all has been called the object to be known of knowledge, O king.

sanskrit: jñānam avyaktam ity uktaṃ jñeyaṃ vai pañcaviṃśakam tathaiva jñānam avyaktaṃ vijñātā pañcaviṃśakaḥ
english: Knowledge is called the Unmanifest, while the object to be known is the twenty-fifth; and so again the Unmanifest is the knowledge, while the knower is the twenty-fifth.

sanskrit: vidyāvidyārthatattvena mayoktaṃ te viśeṣataḥ akṣaraṃ ca kṣaraṃ caiva yad uktaṃ tan nibodha me
english: In the truth of the meaning of Knowledge and Ignorance I have told you in detail; now learn from me what is meant by the Imperishable and the Perishable.

sanskrit: ubhāv etau kṣarāv uktāv ubhāv etau ca nakṣarau kāraṇaṃ tu pravakṣyāmi yathā khyātau tu tattvataḥ
english: Both these have been called perishable, and both these also imperishable; but I shall declare the reason why they are so set forth in truth.

sanskrit: anādinidhanāv etāv ubhāv eveśvarau matau tattvasaṃjñāv ubhāv etau procyete jñānacintakaiḥ
english: Both these are held to be without beginning and without end, both indeed lords; both are spoken of as bearing the name of true principle by those who ponder knowledge.

sanskrit: sargapralayadharmitvād avyaktaṃ prāhur akṣaram tad etad guṇasargāya vikurvāṇaṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: Because it is subject to creation and dissolution, they call the Unmanifest perishable; for it transforms itself again and again for the creation of the qualities.

sanskrit: guṇānāṃ mahadādīnām utpadyati parasparam adhiṣṭhānāt kṣetram āhur etat tat pañcaviṃśakam
english: It gives rise, one from another, to the qualities beginning with the Great Principle; and because it presides over them, this twenty-fifth is called the Field.

sanskrit: yadā tu guṇajālaṃ tad avyaktātmani saṃkṣipet tadā saha guṇais tais tu pañcaviṃśo vilīyate
english: But when it draws that net of qualities back into the Unmanifest as its self, then together with those qualities the twenty-fifth dissolves away.

sanskrit: guṇā guṇeṣu līyante tadaikā prakṛtir bhavet kṣetrajño 'pi yadā tāta tatkṣetre saṃpralīyate
english: The qualities merge into the qualities, and then Prakṛti alone remains; and when, my son, even the Knower of the Field dissolves into that Field —

sanskrit: tadākṣaratvaṃ prakṛtir gacchate guṇasaṃjñitā nirguṇatvaṃ ca vaideha guṇeṣu prativartanāt
english: then Prakṛti, named after the qualities, attains imperishability; and from the withdrawal of the qualities, O prince of Videha, it attains the state of being without qualities.

sanskrit: evam eva ca kṣetrajñaḥ kṣetrajñānaparikṣaye prakṛtyā nirguṇas tv eṣa ity evam anuśuśruma
english: And just so the Knower of the Field, when the knowledge of the Field is exhausted, becomes through Prakṛti free of qualities — thus have we heard it taught.

sanskrit: kṣaro bhavaty eṣa yadā tadā guṇavatīm atha prakṛtiṃ tv abhijānāti nirguṇatvaṃ tathātmanaḥ
english: When this one becomes perishable, it then comes to recognize Prakṛti as endowed with qualities, and likewise the quality-less nature of its own Self.

sanskrit: tadā viśuddho bhavati prakṛteḥ parivarjanāt anyo 'ham anyeyam iti yadā budhyati buddhimān
english: Then he becomes wholly pure through the abandonment of Prakṛti, when the wise one knows, 'I am one thing, and she is another.'

sanskrit: tadaiṣo 'nyatvatām eti na ca miśratvam āvrajet prakṛtyā caiva rājendra namiśro 'nyaś ca dṛśyate
english: Then he attains to separateness and no longer falls into commingling; and with Prakṛti, O lord of kings, he is seen as unmingled and other.

sanskrit: yadā tu guṇajālaṃ tat prākṛtaṃ vijugupsate paśyate cāparaṃ paśyaṃ tadā paśyan na saṃjvaret
english: But when he comes to loathe that net of qualities born of Prakṛti, and beholds the Other as the seer, then, seeing, he is no longer consumed by fever.

sanskrit: kiṃ mayā kṛtam etāvad yo 'haṃ kālam imaṃ janam matsyo jālaṃ hy avijñānād anuvartitavāṃs tathā
english: 'What have I done all this while, I who through all this time have followed birth after birth, as a fish, through want of knowledge, follows the net!'

sanskrit: aham eva hi saṃmohād anyam anyaṃ janāj janam matsyo yathodakajñānād anuvartitavān iha
english: 'For I myself, through delusion, have pursued one birth after another from birth to birth, as a fish, mistaking the net for water, follows after it here.'

sanskrit: matsyo 'nyatvaṃ yathājñānād udakān nābhimanyate ātmānaṃ tadvad ajñānād anyatvaṃ caiva vedmy aham
english: 'As a fish, through ignorance, does not perceive its distinctness from the water, so I, through ignorance, fail to know my own Self and its separateness.'

sanskrit: mamāstu dhig abuddhasya yo 'haṃ magnam imaṃ punaḥ anuvartitavān mohād anyam anyaṃ janāj janam
english: 'Shame upon me, the unawakened, who, sunk again in this, have through delusion pursued one birth after another, from birth to birth!'

sanskrit: ayam atra bhaved bandhur anena saha mokṣaṇam sāmyam ekatvam āyāto yādṛśas tādṛśas tv aham
english: 'This other here shall be my kinsman; with this one comes my liberation. Having come to equality and oneness, I am of the same nature as he.'

sanskrit: tulyatām iha paśyāmi sadṛśo 'ham anena vai ayaṃ hi vimalo vyaktam aham īdṛśakas tathā
english: 'I see here an equality: I am indeed like unto him; for he is stainless and manifest, and I too am even such as he.'

sanskrit: yo 'ham ajñānasaṃmohād ajñayā saṃpravṛttavān sasaṅgayāhaṃ niḥsaṅgaḥ sthitaḥ kālam imaṃ tv aham
english: 'I, who through the delusion of ignorance entered into activity with the unknowing one — I, unattached, have dwelt all this time with her who is attached.'

sanskrit: anayāhaṃ vaśībhūtaḥ kālam etaṃ na buddhavān uccamadhyamanīcānāṃ tām ahaṃ katham āvase
english: 'Brought under her power, I did not awaken all this time. How shall I dwell with her any longer, the cause of high, middling, and low estates?'

sanskrit: samānayānayā ceha sahavāsam ahaṃ katham gacchāmy abuddhabhāvatvād eṣedānīṃ sthiro bhave
english: 'How could I, in my unawakened condition, have come into this dwelling-together with her? Now at last let me be steadfast.'

sanskrit: sahavāsaṃ na yāsyāmi kālam etad dhi vañcanāt vañcito 'smy anayā yad dhi nirvikāro vikārayā
english: 'No longer will I enter into dwelling with her; for all this time I have been deceived. I, the changeless, have been deceived by her who is full of change.'

sanskrit: na cāyam aparādho 'syā aparādho hy ayaṃ mama yo 'ham atrābhavaṃ saktaḥ parāṅmukham upasthitaḥ
english: 'Yet this is no fault of hers; the fault herein is mine, who became attached here and turned my face away from the truth.'

sanskrit: tato 'smi bahurūpāsu sthito mūrtiṣv amūrtimān amūrtaś cāpi mūrtātmā mamatvena pradharṣitaḥ
english: 'Hence, formless, I have dwelt within manifold embodied forms; and though formless, I have taken on a bodied self, overpowered by the sense of "mine."'

sanskrit: prakṛter anayatvena tāsu tāsv iha yoniṣu nirmamasya mamatvena kiṃ kṛtaṃ tāsu tāsu ca yonīṣu vartamānena naṣṭasaṃjñena cetasā
english: 'Through the leadership of Prakṛti, dwelling in this womb and that, what has been done to me — to one free of "mine" — by the sense of "mine," as I passed through womb after womb with a mind whose awareness was lost!'

sanskrit: na mamātrānayā kāryam ahaṃkārakṛtātmayā ātmānaṃ bahudhā kṛtvā yeyaṃ bhūyo yunakti mām idānīm eṣa buddho 'smi nirmamo nirahaṃkṛtaḥ
english: 'I have no further business here with her, whose very self is made of the I-sense, who, making herself manifold, would yoke me to herself again and again. Now have I awakened, free of "mine," free of the I-sense.'

sanskrit: mamatvam anayā nityam ahaṃkārakṛtātmakam apetyāham imāṃ hitvā saṃśrayiṣye nirāmayam
english: 'Casting off the sense of "mine" ever wrought by her through the I-sense, and forsaking her, I shall take refuge in the One free of all affliction.'

sanskrit: anena sāmyaṃ yāsyāmi nānayāham acetasā kṣamaṃ mama sahānena naikatvam anayā saha evaṃ paramasaṃbodhāt pañcaviṃśo 'nubuddhavān
english: 'With him I shall attain equality, not with this unconscious one; fitting for me is union with him, not oneness with her.' Thus, through supreme awakening, the twenty-fifth comes to enlightenment.

sanskrit: akṣaratvaṃ niyaccheta tyaktvā kṣaram anāmayam avyaktaṃ vyaktadharmāṇaṃ saguṇaṃ nirguṇaṃ tathā nirguṇaṃ prathamaṃ dṛṣṭvā tādṛg bhavati maithila
english: He attains imperishability, the unafflicted, abandoning the perishable — the Unmanifest, whose nature is to become manifest, both with qualities and without. Having first beheld the Quality-less, he becomes such as It, O prince of Mithilā.

sanskrit: akṣarakṣarayor etad uktaṃ tava nidarśanam mayeha jñānasaṃpannaṃ yathāśrutinidarśanāt
english: This demonstration of the Imperishable and the Perishable, replete with knowledge, has been told to you by me here, according to the testimony of sacred tradition.

sanskrit: niḥsaṃdigdhaṃ ca sūkṣmaṃ ca vibuddhaṃ vimalaṃ tathā pravakṣyāmi tu te bhūyas tan nibodha yathāśrutam
english: What is free of doubt, subtle, enlightened, and stainless I shall declare to you yet further; learn it as it has been heard.

sanskrit: sāṃkhyayogau mayā proktau śāstradvayanidarśanāt yad eva śāstraṃ sāṃkhyoktaṃ yogadarśanam eva tat
english: Sāṃkhya and Yoga have been expounded by me from the testimony of the two scriptures; and that very teaching declared in Sāṃkhya is itself the doctrine of Yoga.

sanskrit: prabodhanakaraṃ jñānaṃ sāṃkhyānām avanīpate vispaṣṭaṃ procyate tatra śiṣyāṇāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: The awakening knowledge of the followers of Sāṃkhya, O lord of the earth, is therein set forth with full clarity, out of desire for the good of disciples.

sanskrit: bṛhac caiva hi tac chāstram ity āhuḥ kuśalā janāḥ asmiṃś ca śāstre yogānāṃ punar dadhi punaḥ śaraḥ
english: And the skilled declare that scripture to be vast; yet in this scripture of the followers of Yoga it is, as it were, curds again and arrow again — set forth ever afresh.

sanskrit: pañcaviṃśāt paraṃ tattvaṃ na paśyati narādhipa sāṃkhyānāṃ tu paraṃ tatra yathāvad anuvarṇitam
english: Beyond the twenty-fifth they see no further principle, O ruler of men; for the followers of Sāṃkhya, the supreme has been there described just as it is.

sanskrit: buddham apratibuddhaṃ ca budhyamānaṃ ca tattvataḥ budhyamānaṃ ca buddhaṃ ca prāhur yoganidarśanam
english: The Awakened, the Unawakened, and the one in the act of awakening, truly considered — the one in the act of awakening and the Awakened — such, they declare, is the teaching of Yoga.

sanskrit: vasiṣṭha uvāca aprabuddham athāvyaktam imaṃ guṇavidhiṃ śṛṇu guṇān dhārayate hy eṣā sṛjaty ākṣipate tathā
english: Vasiṣṭha said: Now hear of the Unmanifest, the Unawakened, and this ordering of the qualities; for she upholds the qualities, sends them forth, and withdraws them again.

sanskrit: ajasraṃ tv iha krīḍārthaṃ vikurvantī narādhipa ātmānaṃ bahudhā kṛtvā tāny eva ca vicakṣate
english: Ceaselessly here, for the sake of play, transforming herself, O ruler of men, and making her self manifold, she beholds those very forms.

sanskrit: etad evaṃ vikurvāṇāṃ budhyamāno na budhyate avyaktabodhanāc caiva budhyamānaṃ vadanty api
english: Her, thus transforming herself, the one in the act of awakening does not yet comprehend; and because of his awareness of the Unmanifest, they call him the one in the act of awakening.

sanskrit: na tv eva budhyate 'vyaktaṃ saguṇaṃ vātha nirguṇam kadā cit tv eva khalv etad āhur apratibuddhakam
english: Yet he does not comprehend the Unmanifest, whether with qualities or without; and therefore at times indeed they call this Unmanifest the Unawakened.

sanskrit: budhyate yadi vāvyaktam etad vai pañcaviṃśakam budhyamāno bhavaty eṣa saṅgātmaka iti śrutiḥ
english: If the twenty-fifth comes to comprehend this Unmanifest, he becomes the one in the act of awakening, yet still of the nature of attachment — so runs the sacred word.

sanskrit: anenāpratibuddheti vadanty avyaktam acyutam avyaktabodhanāc caiva budhyamānaṃ vadanty uta
english: On this account they call the unfailing Unmanifest the Unawakened; and because of his awareness of the Unmanifest, they call him the one in the act of awakening.

sanskrit: pañcaviṃśaṃ mahātmānaṃ na cāsāv api budhyate ṣaḍviṃśaṃ vimalaṃ buddham aprameyaṃ sanātanam
english: And that twenty-fifth, the great Self, does not yet comprehend the twenty-sixth — the stainless, the Awakened, the immeasurable, the eternal.

sanskrit: satataṃ pañcaviṃśaṃ ca caturviṃśaṃ ca budhyate dṛśyādṛśye hy anugatam ubhāv eva mahādyutī
english: But the twenty-sixth ever comprehends both the twenty-fifth and the twenty-fourth; for he pervades both the seen and the unseen — both, those of great splendor.

sanskrit: avyaktaṃ na tu tad brahma budhyate tāta kevalam kevalaṃ pañcaviṃśaṃ ca caturviṃśaṃ na paśyati
english: But the Unmanifest does not comprehend that Brahman, the Absolute, my son; the twenty-fifth alone does not behold the twenty-fourth as the Absolute.

sanskrit: budhyamāno yadātmānam anyo 'ham iti manyate tadā prakṛtimān eṣa bhavaty avyaktalocanaḥ
english: As long as the one awakening thinks of himself, 'I am other,' so long is he still possessed of Prakṛti, with his vision fixed upon the Unmanifest.

sanskrit: budhyate ca parāṃ buddhiṃ viśuddhām amalāṃ yadā ṣaḍviṃśo rājaśārdūla tadā buddhatvam āvrajet
english: But when he comes to know the supreme Intelligence, wholly pure and stainless — the twenty-sixth — then, O tiger among kings, he attains to the state of the Awakened.
